Copper-Catalyzed Cross-Nucleophile Coupling of β‑Allenyl Silanes
with Tertiary C −H Bonds: A Radical Approach to Branched 1,3-
Dienes
Qi-Chao Shan, Lu-Min Hu, Wei Qin, and Xu-Hong Hu *
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 6041 −6045 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: Described herein is a distinctive approach to branched 1,3-dienes
through oxidative coupling of two nucleophilic substrates, β-allenyl silanes, and
hydrocarbons appending latent functionality by copper catalysis. Notably, C(sp 3)−
H dienylation proceeded in a regiospeci ﬁc manner, even in the presence of
competitive C −H bonds that are capable of occurring hydrogen atom transfer
process, such as those located at benzylic and other tertiary sites, or adjacent to an
oxygen atom. Control experiments support the intermediacy of functionalized alkyl
radicals.
T
he ongoing pursuit of e ﬃcient and selective methods to
access synthetically useful reagents or intermediates by
chemists has greatly in ﬂuenced the design, synthesis, and
applications of complex molecular sca ﬀolds in chemical
sciences. Allenes are a versatile class of unsaturated substrates
in transition-metal-catalyzed coupling reactions due to their
high and unique reactivity.
1 The presence of two orthogonal
cumulative π bonds in allenes endows them with diverse
characteristics to be quali ﬁed as precursors of alkenyl, allenyl,
allyl, and 1,3-dienyl moieties, as well as in cyclization
reactions.2 Among them, dienylation represents an attractive
strategy for the e ﬃcient incorporation of valuable 1,3-diene
functionality.3 Earlier studies in this ﬁeld typically relied on
organometallic reagents coupled with allenes, 4 largely imped-
ing their economy and applicability. Later, elegant break-
throughs via metal-catalyzed aryl or alkenyl C −H dienylation
with allenes have been independently realized by Glorius, Fu,
Kapur and Volla,
5 where preinstalled directing groups were
required to control the regioselectivity ( Scheme 1 a). Despite
these achievements, oxidative couplings of C(sp 3)−H bonds 6
with allenes toward dienylation still remain a formidable
challenge in terms of selectivity and reactivity. In this regard,
we seek out an appealing radical approach to access alkyl
functionalized 1,3-dienes from readily available allene and
alkane substrates by considering the rich precedence of
oxidative radical transformations.
7
The addition of a carbon-centered radical to π-systems of
allenes is arguably among the most powerful and straightfor-
ward methods to forge C −Cb o n d sf o ri n c r e a s i n gt h e
molecular complexity.
8 It has been established that reactive
vinyl or allylic radical species can be generated through a
selective radical attack to an allene at three positions. The
stability of the in situ formed radicals was crucial to the
following radical-trapping steps, which mostly ended up with
the formation of substituted alkenes via hydro-
9 and
difunctionalization,10 as well as annulation processes ( Scheme
1b).11 In those transformations manifold, the issue of chemo-,
regio-, and stereoselectivities has been a persistent concern. We
envisioned that the relatively more stable allyl radical species

could undergo oxidation and subsequent β-elimination to build
conjugated dienes. To our best knowledge, a method targeting
privileged 1,3-dienes through selective addition of carbon-
centered radicals to allenes has never been disclosed, despite
their versatile applications in organic synthesis.
12
1,3-Dicarbonyl compounds have been recognized by many
research groups including us as the sources of functionalized
sp
3 carbon-centered radicals via single electron oxidation, 13
and recently, our laboratory has documented their use in the
tertiary alkylation of alkenes and alkynes.
14 Features of note in
our protocols include the following: (a) e ﬃcient generation of
tertiary carbon-centered radicals from aliphatic C −H bonds, 15
instead of prefunctionalized substrates, such as halides,
alcohols, carboxylic acids, etc.; 16 (b) incorporation of
functionalized alkyl moiet ies holding the options for
derivatizations; (c) sustainable catalytic systems (using Cu or
Fe) without the need for expensive ligand. Because of the
ubiquitous nature and high importance of conjugated dienes,
we wonder whether this principle could be engaged in radical-
mediated functionalization of reactive allenes to produce 1,3-
dienes. Described herein are the discovery, exploration, and
application of an unprecedented copper-catalyzed oxidative
coupling of allenes with tertiary C −H bonds (Scheme 1c). The
protocol gives rise to the regio- and chemoselective formation
of highly functionalized 1,3-dienes, thus leaving ample room
for further synthetic manipulations.
To assess the feasibility of our expected transformation, we
synthesized a set of allene substrates a ﬃliated with di ﬀerent α-
alkyl substituents, and tested their reactivity ( Scheme 2 ). By
employing commercial diethyl methylmalonate ( 2a) as an alkyl
radical precursor, the coupling product 3aa was produced in
20% yield from α-methyl allene ( 1a′) isomerization
17 by using
CuBr2 as the catalyst and di- tert-butyl peroxide (DTBP) as the
oxidant. Replacement of the methyl group at the α position of
allene with carbinol carbonate ( 1a″) led to no conversion. The
negative outcome implied that nucleophilic allenylation of
malonate might not be involved in this reaction.
18 To our
delight, exposure of allenylmethylsilane ( 1a) to the identical
conditions gave a 44% yield of 3aa. It is known that β-allenyl
silanes often act as versatile nucleophiles which tend to attack
carbonyls, iminiums, or other reactive electrophilic agents via
an S
E2′ pathway.19 This newly developed methodology
unlocks the potential utility of such silicon-based carbon π-
systems for the installation of 1,3-diene motifs in cross-
nucleophile coupling reactions.
20
Once determining the β-allenyl silane 1a as the model
substrate, we centered on evaluating the reaction parameters
with low-cost copper salts. Through extensive screening of
copper salts with di ﬀerent counterions and oxidant states
(Table 1 , entries 1 −6), it was found that CuBr
2 showed the
best performance. Extra addition of phosphine (entry 7) or
nitrogen (entry 8) ligands did not improve the conversion. The
reaction appeared to be sens itive to the temperature
conducted. A dramatically reduced yield of 3aa was observed
at the elevated temperature (80 °C), which was ascribed to the
substantial decomposition of 1a (entry 9). The minimum
appropriate temperature was ascertained to be 60 °C, at which
point 3aa was obtained in an undiminished yield (entries 10
and 11). Increasing the amount of CuBr
2 resulted in an
enhancement to the reactivity (entries 12 −14). The addition
of Cy2NH as base, which usually played a bene ﬁcial role in the
β-elimination process, proved to be deleterious to the reaction
at this time (entry 15). Employing 1a in an excess of
stoichiometry (1.4 equiv) with 2a as a limiting reagent a ﬀorded
3aa in 68% yield (entry 16), which was further improved to
70% upon an increase of DTBP loading (entry 17). An
additional survey of oxidant and solvent choices indicated that
DTBP and DMSO were uniquely e ﬀective (see Tables S1 and
S2 for details).
The established optimal conditions stimulated us to explore
the scope and limitation of various β-allenyl silanes with 2a as
the coupling partner. A satisfactory yield of 3aa (71%) was
maintained while enlarging the reaction to a 1 mmol scale. As
shown in Scheme 3 , a wide range of allenes bearing diverse
substituents on the phenyl ring could be converted to
functionalized 1,3-dienes in moderate to good yields under
simple copper catalysis ( 3ba−3la). Synthetically useful func-
tional groups, such as halides ( 3ea, 3ja, and 3ka), nitrile ( 3fa),
triﬂuoromethyl ( 3ga), nitro ( 3ha), and ester ( 3ia), were well
tolerated. Substitution patterns with electronic di ﬀerentiation
had an inapparent e ﬀect on the e ﬃciency in most cases.
However, decorating sterically encumbered substituents (F
and Me) on the ortho position of the phenyl ring caused a drop
in reaction rate and by means of raising the temperature, the
corresponding products 3ka and 3la could be furnished in 61%

and 34% yields, respectively. Extended π-systems, such as a
naphthyl-conjugated allene, proved to be the viable substrate,
smoothly delivering the desired product 3ma in 70% yield.
Aside from aryl-substituted allenes, a heteroaromatic substrate
also followed the transformation, as evidenced by the facile
production of thiophene-tethered 1,3-diene 3na in 50% yield.
Several allenylmethylsilanes ﬂanked by alkyl chains were well
accommodated, providing the access to the trisubstituted 1,3-
dienes ( 3oa−3qa)i n5 5 −67% yields with high regio- and
stereoselectivities. Unfortunately, benzyl-substituted allene, as
the example of less activated aliphatic allenes, was incompatible
with this coupling under the present conditions ( 3ra).
Next, we investigated the chemical diversity of tertiary
C(sp
3)−H bonds that could be selectively functionalized in
Cu-catalyzed dienylation reactions ( Scheme 4 ). The use of
dimethyl methylmalonate did not alter the reactivity, a ﬀording
3ab in 64% yield. Pleasingly, the coupling partners could be
successfully extended to α-substituted malonates appended
with ethyl, benzyl, keto, ﬂuoro, cycloalkyl, ester, and silyl ether
groups, yielding the desired products ( 3ac−3aj) with similar
eﬃciency. It should be mentioned that substrates possessing
competitive aliphatic C −H bonds that are able to undergo a
hydrogen atom transfer process, for example of those located at
benzylic and other tertiary sites, α-keto carbon center, or even
adjacent to an oxygen atom, are all applicable in these oxidative
coupling reactions. Remarkably, the scope of C(sp
3)−H bonds
could be extended to analogous methine carbons attached to
other electron-withdrawing groups, such as ketone, nitrile, and
arylsulfonyl functionalities. The coupling allowed the assembly
of tertiary alkyl substituted 1,3-dienes in up to 75% yield
(3ak−3ao). In addition, the parent 2-alkyl malononitriles
reacted with 1a in a chemospeci ﬁc manner ( 3ap and 3aq),
further underlining the robustness of this protocol.
We then sought to illustrate the postsynthetic utility of the
resultant 1,3-dienes through a series of derivatization reactions
(Scheme 5 ). Intermolecular Diels −Alder reactions of buta-
diene 3aa with several dienophiles, such as N-phenyl-
maleimide, maleic anhydride, and tetracyanoethylene in
toluene, provided cycloadducts 4−6 in excellent yields.
Moreover, the 1,3-diester moiety of 3aa could be readily
transformed into 1,3-diol 7 upon LiAlH
4 reduction. The value
of aryl substituted 1,3-diene was further showcased by the
downstream preparation of indene 8 via a Lewis acid mediated
intramolecular cyclization.
21
Finally, several control experiments were carried out to
elucidate the mechanism. No alkylated product was detected in
the absence of either copper salt or DTBP oxidant.
Subsequently, radical trapping experiments were performed
with 3 equiv of 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidine N-oxide
(TEMPO) or 1 equiv of 2,6-di- tert-butyl-4-methylphenol
(BHT) being added to the standard conditions. As expected,
the coupling between 1a and 2a was strongly suppressed.
Instead, the adduct 9 of alkyl radical trapping was formed in
86% yield, suggesting the involvement of alkyl radical
intermediates in this event ( Scheme 6 a).
On the basis of the above results and literature
precedence,
13,14,22 we propose a plausible reaction pathway
shown in Scheme 6b. The coupling starts by thermal homolysis
of DTBP to generate tert-butoxyl radicals, which abstracts a
hydrogen atom from 2a to form the electrophilic 1,3-diester
radical species A. When the previous observations in catalysts
screening are considered, it can be rationalized that
coordination of CuBr
2 as a Lewis acid with the diester
functionality may occur to facilitate the generation of species
A.

carbon of 1a forms an allylic radical intermediate B, which is
simultaneously stabilized by benzylic conjugation. The
presence of an aryl group had a crucial e ﬀect on the stability
of the radical species according to the inactivity of allene 2r.
The radical B is oxidized by Cu II to produce an allylic
carbocation C along with Cu I via a single electron transfer
(SET) process. Meanwhile, a second SET event from tert-
butoxyl radical occurs to regenerate Cu II species. Intermediate
C undergoes a β-Si elimination with the aid of a tert-butoxyl
anion to deliver the ﬁnal product 3aa. Clearly, formation of a
side-product TMSOtBu of the process can be validated by GC-
MS analysis (see the Supporting Information ).
In conclusion, a mechanistically distinct, practical strategy
for the cross-nucleophile coupling of β-allenyl silanes with
tertiary C −H bonds has been described. By using simple
copper catalytic systems without the use of a ligand or additive,
the reaction provides a regio- and chemoselective approach to
value-added branched 1,3-dienes harboring a diverse collection
of functionalized tertiary alkyl motifs, which were usually
tortuous to access. Mechanistic investigations suggest the
intermediacy of tertiary alkyl radicals. Product modi ﬁcation
allowing for the assembly of carbocycle sca ﬀolds further
broadened the chemical space of this methodology. We
anticipate the potential utility of silicon-based unsaturated
molecules being reported in the context of radical chemistry.
